title: Contest Lifecycle State Diagram
purpose: Document the contest lifecycle states and transitions from draft through active, completed, or canceled, highlighting the auto-complete gap
audience: Backend developers, creator experience engineers, QA engineers, product managers
description: The contest lifecycle has four states: draft (initial state when creator creates contest with start_date and end_date in the future — not visible to fans), active (creator publishes the contest — fans can view and enter during the entry period between start_date and end_date), completed (creator manually finalizes by selecting a winner — no further entries accepted), and canceled (creator can cancel from draft or active states; no mechanism to refund entry fees in current implementation). A notable gap is the absence of auto-complete: when end_date passes, the contest stays active and the creator must manually finalize. Additionally, canceling during the active period has no refund mechanism for entry fees.

actors.label: Creator
actors.description: Content creator who creates, publishes, finalizes, or cancels contests

actors.label: Fan
actors.description: Fan who views and enters active contests

systems.label: Supabase PostgreSQL
systems.description: Database storing contests and contest_entries tables with status transitions

modules.label: contest.service.ts
modules.description: Contest lifecycle logic: create, publish, finalize (winner selection), cancel, enter

modules.label: contest.model.ts
modules.description: Database access for contests and contest_entries tables

modules.label: contest.controller.ts
modules.description: Request handling for contest CRUD and entry operations

services.label: ContestService
services.description: Manages contest lifecycle: draft→active→completed, draft→canceled, active→canceled

dataStores.label: contests table
dataStores.description: Stores contest records with creator_id, title, description, start_date, end_date, entry_requirements (JSONB), entry_type, entry_multiplier, spend_threshold, additional_entries, status (draft|active|completed|canceled), winner_id

dataStores.label: contest_entries table
dataStores.description: Stores entry records with contest_id, fan_id, created_at (unique on contest_id + fan_id)

entryPoints.label: POST /api/v1/contests
entryPoints.description: Creator creates contest with title, start_date, end_date, entry requirements, prize description (protectAndCreator)

entryPoints.label: PUT /api/v1/contests/:id/publish
entryPoints.description: Creator publishes draft contest — makes it visible to fans for entries (protectAndCreator)

entryPoints.label: POST /api/v1/contests/:id/finalize
entryPoints.description: Creator finalizes contest by selecting winner — triggers winner selection algorithm (protectAndCreator)

entryPoints.label: Creator cancels contest
entryPoints.description: Creator can cancel from draft or active state (via status update)

exitPoints.label: Contest completed with winner
exitPoints.description: Winner selected, contest finalized — terminal state

exitPoints.label: Contest canceled
exitPoints.description: Contest cancelled — no entries accepted, no refund mechanism

preconditions: Creator has completed onboarding and has creator role
For entry: fan has active subscription to the creator (if entry_requirements specify)
For publish: contest is in draft state with valid start_date > now and end_date > start_date
postconditions: Contest transitions to new state based on creator action
Completed contest has winner_id set; no further entries accepted
Canceled contest does not accept entries but has no entry fee refund mechanism

nodes.label: [*] → draft
nodes.description: Initial state. Creator creates contest via POST /api/v1/contests with title, start_date, end_date, and entry requirements. Contest is not visible to fans.

nodes.label: draft
nodes.description: Contest in draft mode. Not visible to fans. Creator can edit, publish (→active), or cancel (→canceled).

nodes.label: draft → active
nodes.description: Creator publishes contest via PUT /api/v1/contests/:id/publish. Status changes from draft to active. Contest becomes visible to fans.

nodes.label: active
nodes.description: Contest is active. Fans can view and enter during the entry period (start_date to end_date). Creator can finalize (→completed) or cancel (→canceled). Note: if end_date passes, contest stays active — no auto-transition to completed.

nodes.label: active → completed
nodes.description: Creator finalizes contest by selecting winner via POST /api/v1/contests/:id/finalize. Status changes from active to completed. Winner announcement triggered.

nodes.label: completed
nodes.description: Terminal state. No further entries accepted. Winner announced in contest UI. No re-open supported.

nodes.label: draft → canceled
nodes.description: Creator cancels contest while in draft state. Status changes from draft to canceled. No entries were accepted (was not visible).

nodes.label: active → canceled
nodes.description: Creator cancels contest during active entry period. Status changes from active to canceled. No refund mechanism for any entries that were submitted.

nodes.label: canceled
nodes.description: Terminal state. Contest cancelled. No entries accepted. No mechanism to refund entry fees in current implementation.

nodes.label: active → active (end_date passes)
nodes.description: When end_date passes, contest remains active. No auto-transition to completed. Creator must manually finalize via UI.

errorPaths.destination: Contest stays active; creator must manually finalize
errorPaths.recovery: Creator receives no notification; fans cannot see winner until manual action

errorPaths.trigger: Cancel during active — no entry refund
errorPaths.destination: Contest canceled but entries already submitted have no refund mechanism
errorPaths.recovery: No refund mechanism exists; creator may need to manually handle refunds off-platform

errorPaths.trigger: Winner selection uses Math.random() — not cryptographically secure
errorPaths.destination: Winner selection may be predictable or manipulable
errorPaths.recovery: Not addressed in current implementation — should use cryptographically secure random

errorPaths.trigger: No audit trail for winner selection
errorPaths.destination: No record of random seed, algorithm inputs, or selected winner's probability
errorPaths.recovery: Cannot verify fairness of winner selection after the fact

validationRules: Creator must have protectAndCreator middleware for create, publish, finalize, cancel
Contest must have title, start_date, end_date
For entry: contest must be in active state and end_date not passed
For publish: contest must be in draft state
For finalize: contest must be in active state and not already completed
Unique constraint on (contest_id, fan_id) prevents double entry
businessRules: No auto-complete when end_date passes — creator must manually finalize
No refund mechanism for entry fees when contest is canceled during active period
Winner selection is not cryptographically secure (uses Math.random())
No audit trail for winner selection randomness
Canceled state is terminal — no re-activation route
securityConsiderations: Fan entry requires subscription check (entry_requirements.tier_id or all_subscribers)
Winner selection not cryptographically secure — potential manipulation risk
No audit trail for winner selection — cannot verify fairness
Canceled contest entries contain user data that persists in DB
performanceConsiderations: Winner selection queries transactions table for weighted_spend algorithm — may be slow for entrants with many transactions
Standard algorithm (random) is O(1) — very fast
Weighted_spend algorithm is O(n) where n = total tickets (entrants × tickets per entrant) — potentially large array in memory

annotations.label: ⚠️ No Auto-Complete
annotations.description: When end_date passes, contest stays active. Creator must manually finalize. No automatic transition or notification.

annotations.label: ⚠️ No Cancel Refund
annotations.description: If canceled during active period, there is no mechanism to refund entry fees.

annotations.label: No crypto-safe random
annotations.description: Winner selection uses Math.random() instead of crypto.getRandomValues() or similar.

annotations.label: No audit trail
annotations.description: Winner selection randomness has no audit trail — seed and inputs not recorded.
